title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participates in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra
subtitle:
Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas celebrates the rich heritage, culture and contributions of India's tribal communities: PM

The tradition of celebrating Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, initiated on November 15, 2021, has today transformed into a national festival: PM

There was a time when many days and festivals in our country were determined from a foreign perspective. But today, India is remembering its heritage, its history, and its heroes with indigenous pride; This is a symbol of a major change in our national consciousness: PM

The nation's two monumental achievements are currently the topic of discussion everywhere; The first is the historic triumph over extreme poverty for nearly 50 crore citizens; The second is the country's absolute liberation from the menace of Naxalism, Maoist terror: PM

We have focused especially on those regions that had remained left behind in development for a long time; Special drives were launched in over 100 Aspirational Districts and more than 500 Aspirational Blocks across the country, which include a large number of tribal-populated areas;  Now, under the PM Krishi Dhan Dhanya Yojana, special focus is also being laid on 100 agriculturally backward districts: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 NOV 2026 2:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra via video conferencing, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for 246 development projects worth around ₹3,000 crore. Addressing the gathering on the occasion of the 151st birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda, the Prime Minister greeted citizens across the nation with ‘Johar’, bowed in reverence to Bhagwan Birsa Munda, and stated that the nationwide celebrations reflect the pride of tribal communities and his enduring inspiration as the country remembers its tribal heroes and heroines. Highlighting the grand celebration in Maharashtra's Gadchiroli,a land of rich tribal culture associated with the heroic sagas of Raghoji Bhangre, Bhagoji Naik, and Veer Baburao Shedmake,he bowed to all tribal warriors. “I also felicitate all the Governors, Chief Ministers, Deputy Chief Ministers, and every public representative who are participating in this event from across the country,” said Shri Modi.
Noting that the observance of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, initiated on November 15, 2021, has evolved into a national festival that witnessed over two lakh events and the participation of crores of citizens during Bhagwan Birsa Munda's 150th birth anniversary last year. “Today India is remembering its heritage, its history, and its heroes with Swadeshi self-respect, which is a symbol of a major transformation that has come in our national consciousness,” observed PM Modi.
Recalling how tribal communities consistently raised their voices against colonial injustice,from Tirot Sing's struggle in the Khasi Hills, the Kol movement of Chota Nagpur, and the Santhal revolution led by Sido-Kanhu to the sacrifices of Govind Guru's followers at Mangarh and the courage of Rani Gaidinliu, Tantya Bhil, Alluri Sitarama Raju, and Rani Durgavati, the Prime Minister highlighted the overarching legacy of these freedom movements. “Along with all these sagas, the Ulgulan of Bhagwan Birsa Munda and his struggle at a young age is even today a very big inspiration for crores of us countrymen,” remarked Shri Modi.
Highlighting the inauguration of over 170 tribal development projects and the laying of foundation stones for more than 70 projects worth around 3,000 crore rupees across various states on Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, the Prime Minister noted the inauguration of a museum dedicated to freedom fighter Ropuiliani in Mizoram and the new building of the Tribal Research Institute in Arunachal Pradesh, alongside educational institutions, healthcare services, tribal product marketing centers, and rural infrastructure works. “I extend my heartiest congratulations to the country for all these projects,” affirmed PM Modi.
Observing that this year's celebration coincides with widespread discussion of two historic national milestones,nearly 50 crore citizens defeating extreme poverty and India achieving freedom from Naxalism and Maoist terror, the Prime Minister emphasized the significance of both accomplishments for tribal regions. “Both these achievements are deeply connected with the lives of our tribal brothers and sisters,” noted Shri Modi.
Referring to the recent World Bank report stating that nearly 50 crore Indians escaped extreme poverty over the past 12 to 13 years, the Prime Minister described this as one of India's greatest post-independence achievements driven not by any single government, but by the collective strength of society, the hard work of every citizen, and targeted Central tribal welfare schemes and decisions. “For this achievement, I extend my heartiest congratulations to all the countrymen, especially to my tribal brothers and sisters,” remarked PM Modi.
Describing the exit of millions from poverty as the fulfillment of a firm resolve to prioritize those deprived of development for decades, the Prime Minister noted that the government deployed its full strength in the most backward tribal regions that lacked basic necessities, allocating over one lakh crore rupees for the PM-JANMAN Yojana and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan. “Our effort was that the families whom facilities reached the latest after independence should now have facilities reached to them the fastest,” asserted Shri Modi.
Detailing the government's commitment to prioritizing the underprivileged by constructing over four crore pucca houses for the poor, electrifying 18,000 villages that had remained in darkness for decades after independence, providing free medical coverage up to five lakh rupees under Ayushman Bharat, and establishing over 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs that brought healthcare to remote tribal pockets, the Prime Minister also highlighted the impact of rural sanitation. “When poor families got toilets and sanitation facilities increased, the risk of numerous diseases also decreased,” noted PM Modi.
Emphasizing that eradicating poverty required expanding income opportunities for poor families, the Prime Minister stated that lakhs of crores of rupees in collateral-free loans were disbursed under the Mudra Yojana, benefiting the poor, Dalits, backward classes, and tribal communities alike. “Through this, a new self-confidence to move forward was born within them,” observed Shri Modi.
Highlighting targeted interventions in regions that had long lagged in development, including a special campaign across more than 100 Aspirational Districts and over 500 Aspirational Blocks with large tribal populations as well as a focused drive across 100 agriculturally backward districts under the PM Krishi Dhan Dhanya Yojana to create new opportunities for farmers, poor families, and tribal communities, the Prime Minister underscored the transformative power of collective effort. “These collective efforts and the mantra of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas gave a new self-confidence to the poor of the country, and crores of poor people demonstrated by defeating poverty,” asserted PM Modi.
Turning to the nation's second major milestone of freedom from Naxalism, which inflicted the greatest harm on tribal communities across Gadchiroli and other tribal belts, the Prime Minister noted that around 125 districts were affected by Naxalism, when hundreds of violent incidents occurred every year and claimed the lives of thousands of innocent people, mostly tribal brothers and sisters. Noting that with the end of Naxalism today, mothers and newly secure sisters are blessing the government while youth once robbed of their childhoods are accessing education and employment, the Prime Minister recalled celebrating Diwali a few days ago with security forces in Chhattisgarh's Bastar, a region people once feared to visit. “In all the formerly Naxal-affected areas, including Gadchiroli, this time on Diwali, along with earthen lamps, the light of hope has also reached the people,” observed PM Modi.
Spotlighting the enthusiastic contribution of tribal communities to India's progress and noting that the nation's highest office is held by a daughter of the tribal community, the Prime Minister expressed the nation's collective pride. “All of us are proud of President Droupadi Murmu ji,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address with best wishes on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, the Prime Minister called upon citizens to draw inspiration from the life of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. “Today is the time that taking inspiration from Bhagwan Birsa Munda, we invest even more of our energy in fulfilling the dream of a Viksit Bharat,” asserted PM Modi.

title: English rendering of PM's address at the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra via Video Conferencing
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 NOV 2026 1:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Johar!
Heartiest greetings to all of you across the country who are connected with this celebration of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. On the birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda, I bow to him with deep reverence. Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas is a national occasion that is linked to the pride of the tribal community and to the inspiration of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. With this same spirit, programmes are being organized across the country today to mark Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. The nation is proudly remembering its tribal heroes and heroines. Especially in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, such a massive gathering is taking place. As far as my eyes can see, there are people everywhere. Gadchiroli has a rich tribal cultural heritage. The heroic stories of Raghuji Bhangare, Bhagoji Naik, and Veer Baburao Shedmake are connected to this land. On this occasion, I respectfully pay tribute to all tribal heroes. I also congratulate all the Governors, respected Chief Ministers, Deputy Chief Ministers, and every public representative participating in this event from across the country.
Friends,
The observance of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, which began on 15 November 2021, has now become a national celebration. Last year, on the 150th birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, more than two lakh programmes were organised across the country. Crores of citizens participated in these events. There was a time when many commemorative days and celebrations in our country were shaped through a foreign perspective. But today, India is proudly remembering its heritage, its history, and its heroes with indigenous self-respect. This is a symbol of a major transformation in our national consciousness.
Friends,
Whether it was Tirot Sing’s struggle in the Khasi Hills, the Kol movement in Chota Nagpur, or the Santhal revolution led by Sidho and Kanho, the tribal community has always raised its voice against injustice. On the land of Mangarh, the followers of Govind Guru made the supreme sacrifice. Rani Gaidinliu, Tantya Bhil, and many other heroes and heroines inspired the nation through their courage. Great personalities such as Alluri Sitarama Raju and Rani Durgavati also energized tribal movements. Alongside all these stories of courage, Bhagwan Birsa Munda’s Ulgulan and his struggle at such a young age continue to inspire crores of Indians even today.
Friends,
On the occasion of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas today, more than 170 projects related to tribal development have been inaugurated across different states of the country, and foundation stones have been laid for more than 70 projects. In Mizoram, a museum dedicated to the great freedom fighter Ropuiliani Ji has been inaugurated. In Arunachal Pradesh, a new building of the Tribal Research Institute has also been inaugurated. In addition, among the projects being inaugurated and launched are educational institutions, healthcare facilities, marketing centres for tribal products, and numerous initiatives related to expanding basic amenities in villages. Across different states of the country, projects worth nearly ₹3000 crore have been inaugurated or had their foundation stones laid. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you and to the people of the country for these projects.
Friends,
Today’s programme is taking place at a time when two major achievements of the country are being discussed everywhere. The first achievement is that nearly 50 crore people have overcome extreme poverty and risen out of it. The second achievement is that the country has become free from Naxalism and Maoist terror. Both these achievements are deeply connected with the lives of our tribal brothers and sisters. A few weeks ago, the World Bank report stated that nearly 50 crore people in India have emerged from extreme poverty over the past 12–13 years. This is a very large number, 50 crore people. I consider this one of the greatest achievements of the country since Independence. This achievement belongs to the entire nation. The credit does not belong to any one government. Behind it is the collective strength of society, the effort and hard work of every citizen. The decisions taken by the central government and the schemes launched for tribal welfare in recent years have also played a major role in this achievement. I congratulate all the citizens of the country, especially my tribal brothers and sisters, for this accomplishment.
Friends,
Such a large number of people rising out of poverty is a major transformation in itself. This transformation is the story of a long journey from resolve to achievement. It has created confidence that India can fulfil its resolutions and that every Indian can achieve great goals. We had taken a pledge that those who had remained deprived of the benefits of development for decades would be given priority. As our resolutions began turning into reality on the ground, a chain of positive changes began to emerge. Our government devoted its full strength to those tribal regions that were among the most backward of the backward, where even the most basic facilities of life had not reached. For the PM-JANMAN Scheme and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan, we allocated a budget of more than ₹1 lakh crore. Our effort was that the families who received facilities the latest after Independence should now receive them the fastest.
Friends,
Priority to the deprived, priority to the deprived, this has been our priority. We built more than four crore permanent houses for poor families across the country. Electricity was provided to 18,000 villages where it had not reached even after so many decades of Independence. Through the Ayushman Bharat scheme, free healthcare worth up to ₹5 lakh was provided. More than 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs were established across the country, allowing healthcare benefits to reach even remote tribal areas. When poor families received toilets and sanitation facilities improved, the risk of many diseases was also reduced.
Friends,
To defeat poverty, it was equally important to increase income opportunities for poor families. Through the Mudra Yojana, we provided collateral-free loans. Under this scheme, assistance worth lakhs of crores of rupees was provided. The benefits of all these schemes reached the poor, reached Dalits, reached backward communities, and reached our tribal brothers and sisters as well. This created a new confidence within them to move forward.
Friends,
We also gave special attention to those areas that had remained behind in development for a long time. A special campaign was launched in more than 100 Aspirational Districts and over 500 Aspirational Blocks for development, better facilities, and protection of citizens’ rights. A large number of these regions have significant tribal populations. Now, under the PM Krishi Dhan Dhanya Yojana, special attention is also being given to 100 districts that are backward in agriculture. Our effort is to create new opportunities for farmers, poor families, and tribal communities in these regions. These collective efforts, and the mantra of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, have given new confidence to the poor of the country, and crores of poor people have succeeded in overcoming poverty.
Friends,
The second achievement that I referred to is freedom from Naxalism and Maoism. The people of Gadchiroli, and of tribal regions across the country, know very well that Naxalite violence caused the greatest harm to our tribal communities. In 2014, nearly 125 districts of the country were affected by Maoism and Naxalism. Hundreds of incidents of violence occurred every year. Thousands of innocent people lost their lives in these incidents. A very large number of them were our tribal brothers and sisters.
But friends,
During that period, the people affected by Maoism and Naxalism, these very brothers and sisters of mine, had been left to their fate by the governments of that era. Their rights had been taken away. Everyone sat in silence and remained quiet. You would be shocked to know that these brothers and sisters from our tribal communities were not even allowed to vote. The governments of that time remained mere spectators and sat with their eyes closed. Maoists and Naxalites would take away small children from poor mothers, and nobody could do anything. Naxalites would abduct the daughters of our homes, and everyone could only watch helplessly in anguish.
Friends,
Now that Maoism and Naxalism have been defeated, those mothers, the mothers and sisters of my tribal community, are showering countless blessings upon us. The sister who now feels safe is blessing us. The child whose childhood was once snatched away is today joining us as a young person. He is receiving opportunities for education and employment. In Chhattisgarh, areas like Bastar, where people were once afraid to go, I myself celebrated Diwali with our security forces in the heart of that region just a short while ago. This Diwali, people in all former Naxal-affected regions, including Gadchiroli, have received not only the light of lamps but also the light of hope.
Friends,
Today, our tribal society, our Janjatiya community, is contributing enthusiastically to the progress of the nation. Today, even the leadership of the country is in the hands of a daughter from the tribal community. We are all proud of President Droupadi Murmu ji.
Friends,
Today is the time for us to draw inspiration from Bhagwan Birsa Munda and devote all our energy to fulfilling the dream of a Developed India. With this call, and while bowing to Bhagwan Birsa Munda, I once again extend my heartfelt greetings to all of you on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. And I urge you that every year, 15th November should be eagerly awaited. The birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, and even more than that, Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, is the pride of the entire nation and the self-respect of the entire nation. Every 15th November, with greater strength than before, with greater enthusiasm than before, and on a greater scale than before, we should continue to celebrate this day. On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, we should keep taking new resolutions and dedicate all our strength towards fulfilling those resolutions within a fixed timeframe. What could not be achieved during so many decades after Independence, we must accomplish within a short period. Once again, as I look at the screen and see people gathered at so many places, I can see the enthusiasm and excitement in all of them. This very sight has become the pride, glory, and grandeur of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. For such a successful effort, all of you from the tribal community deserve congratulations. I wholeheartedly congratulate all of you. I thank all of you very much.
Johar.

content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla will inaugurate the Conference of Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region at Vidhana Soudha, Bengaluru, Karnataka, on Tuesday, 17 November 2026.
The inaugural session will be graced by the Chief Minister of Karnataka, Shri D. K. Shivakumar, who will deliver the Keynote Address. The Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha Shri Harivansh; Deputy Chief Minister of Karnataka, Dr. G. Parameshwara; Speaker, Karnataka Legislative Assembly, Shri G. S. Patil; and Chairperson, CWP India Region, Smt. Daggubati Purandeswari will also grace and address the gathering.
The Chairman, Karnataka Legislative Council, Shri Saleem Ahmed will deliver the Welcome Address, while the Deputy Chairman, Karnataka Legislative Council, Dr. Umashree will propose the Vote of Thanks. Women legislators from Parliament and State/UT Legislatures, along with other distinguished dignitaries, will participate in the Conference.
Theme of the two-day Conference is ‘Strong Foundations, Stronger Voices: Inclusive Cyberspace and Mentorship Pathways for New Women Legislators’. Two Plenary Sessions will be held during the Conference. The first, on ‘Empowering Women Digitally: Safe Cyberspace, Smart Choices’, will take place on 17 November 2026 and focus on enabling women to engage safely and effectively in the digital space. The second, on ‘Capacity Building and Mentorship for Women Legislators’, will be held on 18 November 2026 and explore pathways for strengthening legislative capabilities and supporting women legislators, particularly those newly entering legislative institutions. In a special initiative complementing the broader deliberations, UN Women India will organise a side event on menopause on 17 November 2026. The deliberations will provide an important platform for sharing experiences, exchanging best practices and exploring ways to strengthen the participation and leadership of women legislators through digital empowerment, capacity building and mentorship. The event will provide an important platform to foster awareness, encourage informed dialogue and bring greater attention to women's health, well-being and dignity across different stages of life.
The Conference will conclude on Wednesday, 18 November 2026, with the Valedictory Address by the Governor of Karnataka, Dr. Sudha Yadav. The Chief Minister of Karnataka; Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha; and Chairman, Karnataka Legislative Council, will also address the session. The Chairperson, CWP India Region, will present a statement on the outcome of the Conference. The Speaker, Karnataka Legislative Assembly, will deliver the Welcome Address, while the Deputy Speaker, Karnataka Legislative Assembly, will propose the Vote of Thanks.
The Conference is envisaged as a vibrant forum for dialogue, collaboration and collective reflection, reaffirming the indispensable role of women in strengthening democratic institutions. Through its deliberations on digital inclusion, legislative capacity and intergenerational mentorship, it seeks to advance a more enabling and supportive environment in which women legislators can amplify their voices, enrich parliamentary discourse and contribute meaningfully to the future of democratic governance.

subtitle:

date:

content:
President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu; Vice President of India and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan; Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi; Lok Sabha Speaker, Shri Om Birla; Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Law and Justice and Minister of State of the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal and other distinguished dignitaries paid floral tributes at the statue of Bhagwan Birsa Munda at Prerna Sthal in the Parliament House Complex today, on the occasion of his 151st birth anniversary, observed across India as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.
Bhagwan Birsa Munda, revered as Dharti Aaba, holds a distinguished place in Indian history as a freedom fighter and a champion of tribal rights. Through the Ulgulan movement, he mobilised tribal communities against British colonial rule and exploitation, asserting their rights over water, forests and land. His leadership brought together the struggle for freedom with the defence of tribal identity, cultural dignity and self-respect. His courage, sacrifice and commitment to justice remains an enduring source of inspiration for all and his legacy occupies a place of honour in the nation’s collective memory.
Since 2021, 15 November has been observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas to honour the sacrifices of tribal freedom fighters and to recognise the contributions of tribal communities to India’s freedom struggle and national life. The occasion celebrates their rich history, culture and heritage and reaffirms the nation’s gratitude for their contribution to India’s freedom and progress.
As part of the celebrations, tribal folk artists from various states performed at Prerna Sthal, welcoming the dignitaries with their art forms and showcasing the richness of India’s tribal cultural traditions.
Earlier in the day, Lok Sabha Speaker observed in his message on X, as under:
On the 151st birth anniversary of Dharti Aba Bhagwan Birsa Munda ji—the vibrant symbol of tribal identity, self-respect, and patriotism—bowing in utmost reverence, and extending warm greetings to all citizens on the occasion of Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.
At a young age, through his indomitable courage, visionary thought, and extraordinary leadership qualities, he awakened a new consciousness in tribal society. The 'Ulgulan' (revolt) led by him emerged as a powerful mass movement against the exploitative system, injustice, and oppression of British rule. This struggle was not merely political resistance, but a comprehensive pledge to protect the rights, cultural identity, and social justice of tribal communities over water, forests, and land. By making society aware of its traditions, heritage, and self-respect, he showed the path of unity, organization, and self-reliance.
Bhagwan Birsa Munda ji also spread public awareness against social evils, superstition, and exploitation. His ideals strengthened the sense of self-respect, collective responsibility, and vigilance towards their rights among tribal communities. His struggle underscores the truth that the true strength of any society lies in its cultural roots, community solidarity, and the resolve to protect its existence.
His life is such an inspiring saga of sacrifice, penance, struggle, and public service that will continue to illuminate the values of patriotism, social harmony, and justice for generations to come. Bhagwan Birsa Munda ji’s unique contribution is an invaluable heritage of Indian history. His ideals will continue to inspire us to remain steadfastly committed to the respect, rights, and holistic development of tribal society.

title: Agriculture Pavilion in IITF 2026 Witnesses Massive Footfall
subtitle: Pavilion to remain open every day till November 27, 2026, to showcase its unique display of modern agriculture
date:

                15 NOV 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Agriculture Pavilion set-up by Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (MoA&FW) in the 'India International Trade Fair (IITF)' 2026 has emerged as a major crowd-puller at Pragati Maidan. Commencing from November 13 and to be  continued till November 27th 2026, the pavilion today witnessed  extraordinary public participation. The momentum received a major boost with the visit of the Joint Secretary (Extension), who interacted extensively with exhibitors, farmers, and tech innovators, praising their efforts towards awareness creation about sustainable and modern agriculture.
The theme of the pavilion beautifully reflects the progress of MoA&FW in empowering farmers through farmer-centric  interventions of flagship schemes, technology transfer and direct market linkages from 'Seed to Market'.
Strategic Display of Key initiatives and Achievement of MoA&FW Schemes in Agriculture Pavilion include :
• Digital Agriculture & Public Infrastructure: A cornerstone of the pavilion depicts the live demonstration of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for Agriculture, featuring AgriStack, Decision Support System (DSS) for geospatial intelligence, and AR/VR-based Digital Crop Surveys.
• National Mission on Natural Farming & Core Missions: The pavilion spotlights the shift toward eco-friendly farming with full-scale models on Natural Farming, alongside interactive displays from the Pulses Mission and Oilseeds Development ("Save Oil" campaign), stepping towards self-reliance.
• Millets for Nutrition: Backed by the Directorate of Millets Development, this zone attracts massive crowds to  visualise live seed samples, nutritional education, and counters for processed and value-added millet products, as a super food.
• Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY): A dedicated area showcases the success milestones, and the security net provided by the government's premier Crop Insurance Scheme to millions of Indian farmers.
• Per Drop More Crop (PDMC): Underlining the conservation of water through Micro Irrigation automation set-ups display, high-efficiency water conservation techniques and smart irrigation systems.

Dr. M. L. Jat, Hon’ble Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), visited ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), Bengaluru, on 15 November 2026.
During his visit, he inaugurated the Farmers’ Advanced Training Centre (ATC) and the Centre of Excellence for Genome Editing in Horticultural Crops, including a Biosafety Level-II (BSL-II) Laboratory.
Following the inauguration of the Farmers’ Advanced Training Centre, Dr. Jat interacted with progressive farmers, incubatees, entrepreneurs, nursery owners and practitioners of natural farming who have adopted ICAR-IIHR varieties and technologies. The interaction focused on natural farming practices, innovations in horticulture and strategies to mitigate the impact of El Niño and Super El Niño on horticultural crops. Farmers shared their experiences in adopting climate-resilient practices such as mulching, sprinkler irrigation, border cropping, intercropping with short-duration flower and vegetable crops, and green manuring. These interventions have helped improve crop yield, produce quality and farmers’ income.
Addressing the farmers, Dr. Jat emphasized the importance of encouraging educated youth, engineers and agricultural graduates to actively participate and invest in agriculture and horticulture by adopting scientific innovations. He highlighted the need to integrate modern scientific technologies with traditional wisdom and stressed that farmers must remain at the centre of all agricultural research and development initiatives. He also appreciated the role of ICAR institutions, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes (ATARIs) in popularizing innovative technologies through Government of India programmes, particularly the Khet Bachao Abhiyan (KBA). He assured that successful farmer innovations and experiences would be documented and disseminated widely to benefit farming communities across the country.
Subsequently, Dr. Jat inaugurated the
Centre of Excellence for Genome Editing in Horticultural Crops, equipped with a Biosafety Level-II Laboratory
, marking an important step towards strengthening advanced biotechnology research and genome-editing capabilities in horticultural crops. He emphasized that scientists should prepare for the future by developing self-reliance in genome resources for genome-editing research. He also highlighted the need for prioritization, better targeting, development of a strong data ecosystem and identification of opportunities where Indian agricultural research can achieve global standards and first-of-its-kind innovations.
During his interaction with postgraduate students, he stressed the importance of nurturing young scientific talent and strengthening human capital. He encouraged scientists to move beyond conventional approaches, embrace new opportunities and work towards making agriculture a major contributor to India's vision of a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047, with a targeted contribution of USD 6 trillion from agriculture. He also highlighted the potential of microbial technologies, biofertilizer start-ups and innovations in health and nutrition.
The visit also included interaction with postgraduate students, visits to research laboratories and a field visit to the institute's research facilities. The visit provided an important platform to strengthen the institute's research, innovation, farmer outreach and human resource development initiatives, reaffirming ICAR-IIHR's commitment to sustainable, climate-resilient and technology-driven horticultural development.
On this occasion Dr V B Patel, ADG Fruits and  spices, Director IIHR Dr Tusar Kanti Behera, Directors and Heads of the ICAR institutes in Bengaluru, Scientists of the institute, Postgraduate students, research scholars, Innovative farmers and Agri entrepreneurs were present.

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal arrived in Cairo, Egypt, on 14 November 2026, for an official visit aimed at strengthening the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership, deepening bilateral trade and investment relations, and exploring new opportunities for industrial and commercial cooperation between the two countries.
India and Egypt share a longstanding relationship rooted in historical, civilizational and people-to-people ties. Over the years, this relationship has evolved into a multifaceted partnership encompassing political, economic, security and cultural cooperation. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India–Egypt relations have gained renewed momentum, culminating in the elevation of bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership, with a shared commitment to enhanced cooperation, including in the economic domain.
At the beginning of his visit, Shri Piyush Goyal paid homage to Indian soldiers at the Heliopolis War Cemetery in Cairo, honouring their sacrifice and contribution. Speaking on the occasion, Shri Piyush Goyal highlighted the strength of India–Egypt relations, noting that bilateral trade of around US$6.5 billion represents only the beginning of the partnership between the two ancient civilisations. Describing the Indian community as a living bridge between the two countries, he underscored the contribution of nearly 70 Indian companies operating in Egypt, with investments exceeding US$5 billion and generating direct and indirect employment for Egyptians.
The Indian community in Egypt continues to serve as an important bridge between the two nations, contributing to commercial exchanges, professional cooperation and the broader India–Egypt relationship.
The visit will feature the 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC), the India–Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC) Meeting and the India–Egypt Business Forum. The programme will also include bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers, interactions with leading business representatives and meetings with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), the Egyptian Junior Businessmen Association and the Egypt–India Startups Forum. These engagements are expected to provide platforms for reviewing bilateral economic cooperation, addressing trade and investment-related issues, and identifying new avenues for business partnerships, while giving fresh impetus to bilateral trade, investment, industrial cooperation and innovation linkages.

content:
In a significant initiative towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of 'Sahkar se Samriddhi' and further strengthening, modernising and making the cooperative movement in the country more inclusive, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today performed the Bhoomi Pujan for the revival of NHEC (National Heavy Engineering Cooperative) Multi-State Cooperative Society at Talegaon Dabhade in Pune district, Maharashtra. On the occasion, he also virtually inaugurated the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) and launched Bharat Taxi services in Pune. Deputy Chief Ministers of Maharashtra Shri Eknath Shinde and Smt. Sunetra Ajit Pawar, Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Krishan Pal Gurjar, Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol, Maharashtra Minister for Higher and Technical Education and Parliamentary Affairs Shri Chandrakant Patil, Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani, and several other dignitaries were present at the event.
In his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah paid tribute to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and said that the land of Maharashtra has not only played a significant role in establishing and strengthening the spirit of Swaraj but has also given a new direction to the cooperative movement in the country. He said that Maharashtra, particularly Pune, can rightly be described as the fountainhead of the cooperative movement in western India. Pioneers of the cooperative movement, including Padma Shri Vitthalrao Patil and Vaikunthbhai Mehta, had endeavoured even before Independence to develop a system in which the maximum benefits arising from agriculture and trade would reach farmers.
Shri Amit Shah said that farmers, rural women, milk producers and those associated with the cooperative movement had long been demanding the establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation at the Centre. He said that this demand remained unfulfilled during the tenure of previous governments, while the Central Government under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi established a dedicated Ministry of Cooperation, giving a new direction to the cooperative sector. He said that Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), district-level cooperative institutions and the dairy sector are steadily becoming stronger. The Central Government has undertaken several significant measures, including providing relief of approximately Rs. 15,000 crore to cooperative sugar mills and extending income tax relief of approximately Rs. 3,000 crore annually.
The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that a major manufacturing facility producing machinery and equipment for sugar mills once operated on the very land where today's programme was being held. The factory had ceased operations during the tenure of a previous government. He said that the reconstruction of the same industrial complex is now being initiated, marking an occasion of pride and satisfaction for the cooperative sector.
Shri Amit Shah extended his greetings to the people of the country, particularly mothers and sisters, on the occasion of Chhath Mahaparv. Paying tribute to Bhagwan Birsa Munda on his 151st birth anniversary, he said that Bhagwan Birsa Munda had ignited the spirit of resistance against colonial rule from the land of Jharkhand even before the wider freedom movement gathered momentum. He said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi decided to commemorate the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. Shri Shah also referred to the progress made towards eliminating Naxalism in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, and the programme held there. Paying homage to Acharya Vinoba Bhave, he said that Vinoba Ji dedicated his life to cow welfare, Sarvodaya, the Bhoodan Movement and strengthening Indian languages through the Devanagari script. He recalled that Vinoba Bhave, a devoted follower of Mahatma Gandhi, spent a significant part of his life in Wardha, Maharashtra.
Referring to the inauguration of the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS), the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that a large number of Multi-State Cooperative Societies operate across the western region, including Maharashtra and Gujarat. He said that there had been demands from different regions for the establishment of this office, which has now been set up in Pune. Shri Shah informed that the office would undertake regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Daman and Diu.
Referring to the launch of Bharat Taxi services in Pune, Shri Amit Shah said that cooperative-based Bharat Taxi services would be expanded across the country. He said that for many years, drivers associated with several taxi companies had to surrender a portion of their earnings as commission and, in many instances, faced exploitation. The concept of Bharat Taxi, based on the cooperative model, was developed to address this situation. He said that through Bharat Taxi, the Sarathi brothers and sisters, who were earlier recognised merely as drivers, are now becoming owners of their own company. The system ensures complete transparency, with the entire earnings of Sarathis being credited directly to their bank accounts without any commission deductions. He said that Bharat Taxi services should also be introduced in Nagpur, Nashik, Kolhapur and Solapur after Pune.
The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, referring to the Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC (National Heavy Engineering Cooperative), said that the institution had previously operated from the same location and supplied sugar mills and centrifugal machinery across the world. He said that over time, the industrial unit ceased operations, and its approximately 110 acres of land increasingly faced the threat of illegal encroachment. The Ministry of Cooperation initiated efforts to revive this important cooperative industrial asset and began the process of its restoration with the support of institutions such as the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), Amul, IPL, IFFCO and the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC).
Shri Amit Shah said that the manufacturing facility to be established at NHEC would not be limited to producing sugar mills. It would also manufacture power generation plants for sugar mills, Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants and various types of industrial equipment and plants related to the dairy sector. In addition, the facility would undertake container manufacturing for export to overseas markets. He said that the earnings generated from these industrial activities would accrue to cooperative institutions, thereby further strengthening the cooperative-based economic ecosystem.
The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that there was a time when sugar mills manufactured by NHEC were exported to 11 countries, including Zambia, Ethiopia and Vietnam. The manufacturing facility had such a strong order book and demand that the delivery of new orders could take approximately four years. He said that these industrial operations subsequently came to a halt, but the Central Government has now decided to revive this important cooperative institution.
Shri Amit Shah informed that, as part of the revival process of NHEC, the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) initially took over the management of the institution as its administrator. Subsequently, all audits that had remained pending for the previous two years were completed. Institutions including Amul, NDDB, NCDC, IFFCO, NABARD and IPL contributed towards mobilising the investment required for the revival of the institution. Its Board of Directors was reconstituted, and at its first meeting held on 9 October 2026, a resolution was taken to rebuild the institution. The Bhoomi Pujan of the project was performed today as part of this process.
The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that a plan has been prepared to reschedule all liabilities and loans of NHEC and settle them in a transparent manner. He expressed confidence that production would commence at the facility before December 2027 and manufacturing of sugar mills would resume. He said that a circular economy would also be developed in the sugar and dairy sectors, creating additional income opportunities for farmers through the productive utilisation of resources such as cattle dung. Similarly, efforts would be made to reduce dependence on imports by increasing the utilisation of various by-products generated by sugar mills. He further informed that the second phase of the project envisages manufacturing containers for the railways, defence sector and exports.
Shri Amit Shah expressed confidence that, like successful cooperative institutions such as Amul, IFFCO and KRIBHCO, NHEC would also emerge as an important example for the cooperative movement in the country in the coming years. He congratulated all the institutions associated with the revival of NHEC and the farmers of Maharashtra on this initiative.
In his address, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation also referred to the country's democratic system and the role of political parties, observing that the principal opposition party has faced successive electoral defeats in recent years. Referring to 'Bharat Summit 2026' held in Hyderabad, he said that the remarks made by the Leader of the Opposition at the international conference concerning India's development journey, democratic system and national leadership were inappropriate. Shri Shah said that the electoral success or failure of political parties depends on their leadership, performance and the confidence reposed in them by the people.
Shri Amit Shah referred to the tenure of the previous government and said that several allegations and controversies relating to corruption had emerged during that period, whereas development across various sectors has gained momentum over the past 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He highlighted achievements in agriculture, industrial development, India's historic accomplishment of reaching the Moon's south polar region, expansion of the startup ecosystem, modernisation of the railways, increase in the number of airports to approximately 150, expansion of the metro network, introduction of the National Education Policy and establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation.
The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation advised the Leader of the Opposition that engaging with people in India's villages and understanding their concerns was more important than criticising the country on international platforms. He said that, in a democracy, the path to political power lies in reaching out to the people and earning their trust. Shri Shah said that all political parties, whether in government or in opposition, have a responsibility to safeguard the country's reputation, democratic institutions and national interests on international platforms. He also urged workers of the opposition party to reflect on the approach and political direction of their leadership, adding that the people of the country express their verdict through the democratic process.
Concluding his address, Shri Amit Shah said that a new beginning has been made in the cooperative sector today. Industrial production activities will resume at the approximately 110-acre complex that had remained closed for years. He extended his best wishes to cooperative sector workers and farmers across the country and expressed confidence that the revival of NHEC would give a new direction to cooperative-led industrial development in India.
During the programme, a Letter of Intent (LoI) was exchanged between NHEC and IDMC Limited, and share certificates were presented to Bharat Taxi Sarathis.

title: Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha Arrive at Golden Pagoda, Namsai, Marking the Final Phase of Exposition in Arunachal Pradesh
subtitle:
Governor of Arunachal Pradesh Inaugurates the Exposition at Namsai; Sacred Relics to Remain Open for Public Darshan from 14 to 20 November 2026

Over 35,000 Devotees Pay Homage to the Sacred Relics at Bomdila; Cumulative Footfall at Tawang and Bomdila Exceeds 66,000

Two Special Exhibitions on Buddhist Heritage Inaugurated at Golden Pagoda
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 NOV 2026 7:32AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha arrived at Namsai, Arunachal Pradesh, on 14 November 2026, marking the commencement of the third and final phase of their exposition in the State. The Sacred Relics were ceremonially received and enshrined at the Golden Pagoda (Kongmu Kham), one of the prominent centres of Buddhist faith and heritage in eastern Arunachal Pradesh.
The Governor of Arunachal Pradesh, Lt Gen Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik (Retd.), received the Sacred Relics at Nalung Helipad in Namsai. He was accompanied by Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein, State Ministers, public representatives and religious leaders. Devotees and members of the local community gathered along the ceremonial route to the Golden Pagoda to pay their respects to the Sacred Relics.
The exposition was formally inaugurated at the Golden Pagoda following the reception and enshrinement ceremony. The Governor graced the occasion as the Chief Guest. Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein, Shri Raghav Prasad Bhatnagar, Director General, International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), venerable members of the Buddhist Sangha and other distinguished guests were present on the occasion.
Governor Highlights the Contemporary Relevance of Lord Buddha's Teachings
Addressing the gathering, the Governor described the exposition as an occasion of profound spiritual and cultural significance. He observed that the Sacred Relics symbolise the life, enlightenment and timeless teachings of Lord Buddha.
The Governor highlighted the relevance of Buddhist teachings in addressing contemporary challenges. He noted that the message of peace, compassion, wisdom and non-violence assumes particular significance at a time when humanity faces conflict, intolerance and violence.
He urged people to imbibe these values in their daily lives and contribute to building a society founded on harmony, dignity and mutual respect.
The Governor appreciated the collective efforts of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the National Museum, New Delhi, the International Buddhist Confederation and all those associated with the exposition. He acknowledged their contribution in bringing the Sacred Relics closer to devotees across Arunachal Pradesh.
Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein highlighted the rich and diverse Buddhist heritage of Arunachal Pradesh. He underlined the significance of the exposition in a State where Mahayana, Vajrayana and Theravada Buddhist traditions have flourished across generations. He described the arrival of the Sacred Relics at Namsai as a rare opportunity for devotees to offer prayers and reconnect with the teachings of Lord Buddha.
On the occasion, two special exhibitions organised by the National Museum, New Delhi, and the International Buddhist Confederation were inaugurated at the Meditation Centre of the Golden Pagoda.
The exhibition titled
“Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery”
, organised by the International Buddhist Confederation, presents the historical, archaeological and spiritual significance of the Piprahwa Relics. It traces the archaeological discoveries at Piprahwa in Uttar Pradesh and the enduring tradition of Buddhist relic veneration.
The exhibition also highlights the journey of the Piprahwa jewel collection and its return to India in 2025 after more than a century. It provides visitors with an opportunity to understand the importance of preserving and protecting India's Buddhist heritage.
The second exhibition, titled
“Crossroads of Dhamma: Classical Legacies, Living Art, and Anthropological Perspectives”
, curated by the National Museum, New Delhi, showcases the rich artistic, historical and cultural heritage of Buddhism. It highlights the evolution of Buddhist traditions and their continuing influence on art, culture and society.
Together, these exhibitions complement the spiritual experience of the Sacred Relics Exposition. They offer devotees, students, scholars and visitors an opportunity to deepen their understanding of the life and teachings of Lord Buddha and India's rich Buddhist heritage.
The arrival of the Sacred Relics at Namsai follows the successful conclusion of the six day exposition at Thubchog Gatsel Ling (TGL) Monastery, also known as Lower Gompa, in Bomdila, West Kameng district.
The exposition, held from 8 to 13 November 2026, witnessed an overwhelming response from devotees. More than 35,000 devotees visited the monastery during this period to offer prayers, seek blessings and pay homage to the Sacred Relics.
Buddhist monks, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and devotees from different parts of West Kameng district and neighbouring regions participated in the public darshan with deep faith and reverence.
The district administration made arrangements for constituency wise participation to facilitate orderly public darshan and ensure that devotees from different areas had an opportunity to visit the exposition.
The large turnout at Bomdila reflected the deep spiritual significance of the Sacred Relics and the enduring Buddhist traditions of the region.
Following the conclusion of public darshan on 13 November, the Sacred Relics were accorded a ceremonial farewell on the morning of 14 November for their onward journey to Namsai.
The exposition of the Sacred Relics in Arunachal Pradesh commenced at the historic Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) on 31 October 2026. The inaugural ceremony was attended by Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh Shri Pema Khandu, venerable Buddhist monks and other dignitaries.
The exposition at Tawang continued until 7 November 2026 and witnessed participation by more than 31,000 devotees.
With over 35,000 devotees visiting the subsequent exposition at Bomdila, the cumulative footfall at the two venues has exceeded 66,000.
The return of the Sacred Relics to Arunachal Pradesh after a gap of 13 years has provided Buddhist communities across the State with a cherished opportunity to pay homage to Lord Buddha.
The exposition has brought together devotees from different Buddhist traditions and cultural backgrounds. It has also reaffirmed the enduring spiritual and cultural bonds that connect the people of Arunachal Pradesh with India's wider Buddhist heritage.
The Sacred Relics will remain enshrined at the Golden Pagoda (Kongmu Kham), Namsai, for public darshan from 14 to 20 November 2026.
The Golden Pagoda is an important centre of Theravada Buddhist faith and practice in Arunachal Pradesh. The exposition at Namsai will provide devotees from eastern Arunachal Pradesh and neighbouring regions an opportunity to offer prayers and pay homage to the Sacred Relics.
Following the conclusion of the exposition, the Sacred Relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on 21 November 2026.
The exposition is being organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the National Museum, New Delhi, and the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), New Delhi.
The initiative reflects the Government of India's sustained commitment to the protection, preservation and promotion of India's Buddhist heritage. It seeks to bring this sacred heritage closer to devotees and strengthen cultural and spiritual connections across Buddhist communities.
The exposition at Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai also celebrates the diversity of Buddhist traditions in Arunachal Pradesh and reinforces the universal message of Lord Buddha — peace, compassion, wisdom, non-violence and harmony.

title: MAINTENANCE COMMAND OF IAF REAFFIRMS COMMITMENT TO SOVEREIGN SUSTAINMENT

content:
13 Base Repair Depot, Indian Air Force, celebrated fifty years of distinguished service with a seminar on “Air Defence2040: Sensors, Networks & Sovereign Sustainment” at the Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi. The seminar was presided over by Air Marshal Yalla Umesh, VSM, PhD, Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Maintenance Command and witnessed participation from senior military leadership, veterans, DRDO, academia and leading defence industry partners.
Established in 1976, the Base Repair Depot has been a key pillar of the Indian Air Force’s maintenance ecosystem, undertaking repair, overhaul and life cycle support of critical radar and communication equipment. Tracing its legacy to the Radar and Communication Project Office, the Depot has made significant contributions towards ensuring the operational availability and reliability of vital air defence systems over the last five decades. In his welcome address, Air Officer Commanding of the Depot highlighted the Depot’s journey, acknowledged the contribution of its veterans and emphasised the need to build indigenous engineering and industrial capabilities to meet the evolving requirements of Air Defence 2040.
Addressing the gathering, Air Marshal Yalla Umesh, AOC-in-C, Maintenance Command emphasised that the true effectiveness of an air defence system lies in its operational availability. He highlighted that sustainment must be integral to equipment design and induction, stressing that sovereign sustainment entails the ability to diagnose, repair and restore sophisticated defence systems within the country. He called upon industry partners to develop equipment with indigenous testing, repair and life-cycle support capabilities, reinforcing the vision of self-reliance in defence.
The seminar featured expert deliberations on emerging technologies, including quantum sensing, life-cycle management and modernisation of air defence radars and network-centric air defence.
The seminar also highlighted a significant milestone in sustainable radar operations, with the successful demonstration of hydrogen fuel cell technology for powering IAF radars, in partnership with the National Green Hydrogen Mission and NTPC. The initiative underscores the potential of clean energy solutions to enhance operational resilience, energy autonomy and sustainable deployment of air defence systems, particularly in challenging operational environments.

subtitle:
“Indigenous capabilities in advanced inspection technologies, consistent quality assurance practices & reliability of testing results key to strengthening Non-Destructive Testing ecosystem to enhance defence preparedness & self-reliance”

“Aatmanirbharta in defence is not merely an economic objective but also a strategic necessity”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 NOV 2026 11:52AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called for making India not merely a user of advanced technologies, but also a developer, innovator and global leader in critical domains, emphasising the need to strengthen the country’s Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) ecosystem to enhance defence preparedness and self-reliance. Virtually addressing the 36th Annual Conference on Non-Destructive Evaluation & Enabling Technologies and the 15th International Symposium on Non-Destructive Testing in Aerospace on November 15, 2026, he stressed the importance of developing indigenous capabilities in advanced inspection technologies, promoting consistent quality assurance practices and ensuring the accuracy, reliability and integrity of testing results, particularly in strategic applications. He asserted that there can be no compromise on the integrity of testing results in strategic applications.
“We must strengthen our indigenous capabilities in advanced inspection technologies, specialised sensors, evaluation equipment and associated software. Developing domestic capabilities in these areas is essential for reducing technological dependencies and securing critical defence supply chains. We must promote consistent quality assurance practices across the entire defence industrial ecosystem. Public Sector Undertakings, private manufacturers, start-ups and MSMEs have an important role to play in this endeavour. We must ensure that inspection results are accurate, reliable and traceable, and are based on robust procedures and appropriate standards followed by assessment by qualified professionals,” said Raksha Mantri.
Shri Rajnath Singh stressed that NDT technologies enable examination of the integrity of materials, components and structures without causing any damage to them. Elucidating the concept, he said just as ultrasound and X-rays help examine the human body without surgical intervention, NDT techniques enable the detection of internal defects in critical components without dismantling or damaging them.
Raksha Mantri underlined that as Indian defence systems become increasingly sophisticated, every critical material, component, assembly and manufacturing process must meet the highest standards of quality and reliability. “Hidden defects can affect operational availability, increase maintenance requirements, reduce the service life of equipment and, in critical situations, jeopardise mission success. We need to move beyond a culture of merely identifying defects towards actively preventing them by embedding quality at every stage of the manufacturing process,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh stressed that the progress of a nation depends not merely on the technologies it develops, but also on the quality, reliability and security of the systems it builds. In defence applications, including missiles, aircraft, naval platforms and spacecraft, quality is not merely a manufacturing requirement but an essential element of operational reliability and national security, he said.
Emphasising the strategic significance of the sector, Raksha Mantri stated that for a country aspiring to achieve technological leadership, the importance of NDT cannot be overstated. He asserted that India's pursuit of Aatmanirbharta in defence is not merely an economic objective but also a strategic necessity.
Highlighting India’s growing indigenous defence ecosystem, Shri Rajnath Singh cited achievements in missile development, naval platforms, aerospace engineering, radar systems and space applications as reflections of the expanding scientific and industrial capabilities of the nation. He described the commissioning of India's first indigenous aircraft carrier, INS Vikrant as an important milestone in the Aatmanirbhar Bharat journey.
On the broader significance of innovation, Raksha Mantri stated that it goes beyond scientific discoveries and new inventions, encompassing the continuous improvement, upgrading and enhancement of existing technologies & systems. He highlighted the progress made in promoting innovation in the defence sector through institutional mechanisms and policy initiatives. Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) and the Technology Development Fund (TDF) are important initiatives that have encouraged innovative thinking, technological development and experimentation, giving a new direction to India’s defence ecosystem, he said.
Underscoring the importance of keeping pace with the rapidly changing global security environment, Shri Rajnath Singh said that the indigenous weapons, platforms and supporting systems must deliver the highest levels of reliability and performance at all times. He urged professionals associated with the NDT sector to continuously upgrade their capabilities and keep the spirit of innovation alive in sync with emerging technologies and evolving security requirements.
On the technological transformation underway in the field of Non-Destructive Evaluation, Raksha Mantri stressed that Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics, Advanced Sensors, Digital Twins and Predictive Analytics are significantly expanding the possibilities of inspection and structural health monitoring. These technologies, he said, can improve the speed and consistency of inspections, facilitate the analysis of complex data and identify patterns that may not be easily detectable through conventional methods.
Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that the future lies in the intelligent integration of established inspection techniques with advanced digital technologies to make inspection processes more accurate, efficient and responsive to emerging industrial requirements. He called upon India to move beyond merely adopting these technologies and develop indigenous solutions tailored to its strategic and industrial requirements. Investment in research, advanced equipment, software and skilled manpower would strengthen domestic capabilities and enable Indian technologies to find markets internationally, he said.
Raksha Mantri highlighted that innovation flourishes when Government, Industry, Academia and Research Laboratories work together. He called for a whole-of-government and whole-of-ecosystem approach, with all stakeholders working towards a common objective of technological advancement and strategic self-reliance.
The three-day conference, organised by the Indian Society for Non-Destructive Testing in Hyderabad, Telangana, has brought together over 2,000 professionals, researchers, industry experts and students to deliberate on the latest advancements, emerging technologies and applications in NDT. It has provided a platform for knowledge exchange, technical discussions and collaboration among stakeholders from industry, academia and research institutions, with a focus on strengthening NDT capabilities, promoting innovation and advancing the adoption of cutting-edge inspection and evaluation technologies across sectors, including defence and aerospace.

title: NIELIT to organize 3rd National Conference on Cyber Security, Digital Forensics & Intelligence (NCCDFI 2026) to be held in New Delhi on November 16–17, 2026
subtitle:
NCCDFI 2026 to Bring Together Key Stakeholders to Strengthen India’s Cybersecurity and Digital Forensics Ecosystem

The conference will be held under the theme “Cyber Secure Bharat: Fortifying India’s Digital Future”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 NOV 2026 11:06AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT), under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, is organising the 3rd National Conference on Cyber Security, Digital Forensics & Intelligence (NCCDFI 2026) on November 16-17, 2026, at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, 15 Janpath, New Delhi, centered around the theme “Cyber Secure Bharat: Fortifying India’s Digital Future.
The conference assumes noteworthy significance in the present digital era, wherein the increasing dependence on digital technologies, the emergence of sophisticated cyber threats and the evolving nature of cybercrime have made cyber security and digital investigation critical areas of national importance.
The journey of NCCDFI began in 2024 with its inaugural edition in Kohima, Nagaland, held from 25–26 July 2024 at the Capital Convention Centre, Organised by NIELIT Kohima in collaboration with the Nagaland Police and the Department of Information Technology & Communication, Government of Nagaland. Building on the foundation laid in Kohima, the second edition of NCCDFI was held in 2025 at Gauhati University, Guwahati, Assam. Drawing on the success of its preceding editions, the conference expanded its reach from a regional initiative into a broader national platform. The third edition aims to further strengthen this platform through wider participation, technology demonstrations, knowledge exchange and stronger collaboration among key stakeholders.
NCCDFI 2026 will provide a knowledge-sharing platform for stakeholders from government, law enforcement, defence, judiciary, technology providers, industry, academia and the cybersecurity ecosystem to deliberate on emerging cyber threats and evolving challenges in digital investigations and cyber resilience. The conference will focus on strengthening coordination among agencies, enhancing capacity in cybersecurity and digital forensics, facilitating policy dialogue and exploring the application of emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain Security and Cyber Intelligence.
NCCDFI 2026 is supported by a strong group of industry partners, bringing together leading organisations in digital forensics, cybersecurity and investigative technologies. The knowledge partners includes Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), CERT-In, Delhi Police, CyberPeace, Standardisation Testing and Quality Certification (STQC), Military College of Telecommunication Engineering (MCTE), Mhow, Maharashtra Cyber, Manipur Police, Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TGCSB), Hyderabad, Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) and Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). The industry partners includes STELLAR, Power Forensics & Digital Intelligence, Magnet Forensics, MSAB, Cyint Technologies, 3rd Eye Techno Solutions, Advanced Digital Forensic Solutions, Inc., Oxygen Forensics and VERTEXON LABS. Their participation will contribute industry expertise, technology demonstrations and practical insights, strengthening the conference’s focus on advancing capabilities in cybersecurity, digital forensics and digital investigations.
The conference will focus on 10 key tracks covering the evolving cybersecurity landscape: Cybersecurity, Digital Forensics, AI Security, Critical Infrastructure, Threat Intelligence, Blockchain & Crypto, Drone & IoT Forensics, Digital Evidence, Cyber Law, and Cloud Security. These tracks will bring together experts and practitioners to explore
emerging
threats, technological advancements, investigative techniques, regulatory developments and strategies for building a secure and resilient digital ecosystem.
The two-day conference will feature an inaugural session, technical and business sessions, panel
discussions, an industry
exhibition and Cyber Kushti 2026 – Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon. The technical sessions will cover key areas including national cybersecurity and critical infrastructure, incident response, AI-enabled cyber threats, automated digital investigations, cyber threat intelligence, financial cybercrime, advanced device and multimedia forensics, law-enforcement readiness, international cooperation, digital evidence, quantum computing, autonomous systems, frontier technologies, capacity building and the national cyber ecosystem. The exhibition during the conference will showcase technologies and solutions in digital forensics, cybersecurity, drone technology, surveillance systems and AI-driven security, with opportunities for technical interactions and business-to-business engagements.
A key highlight of NCCDFI 2026, “Cyber Kushti 2026- Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon”, will be organised alongside the technical sessions. The three-level competition is structured around the themes of Review, Attack and Defend, reflecting critical aspects of modern cybersecurity operations. The hackathon has received an overwhelming response, with 1,031 teams comprising 3,093 participants registering for the competition. Of these, 923 teams (2,769 participants) have been shortlisted for Level 1, while 50 teams have qualified for Level 2 and 10 teams for Level 3.
NCCDFI 2026 will also feature the signing of MoUs between NIELIT and industry partners, aimed at strengthening institutional partnership, knowledge exchange, joint initiatives, research and development, and capacity building in the fields of cyber security, digital forensics & intelligence, etc. These collaborations are envisaged to establish a framework for long-term cooperation and facilitate industry-academia engagement and promote future collaborative initiatives in these critical domains.
Through NCCDFI 2026, NIELIT along with its supporting organisations and institutional partners, seeks to contribute towards strengthening professional competencies, fostering institutional collaboration and supporting the development of a secure, resilient and trusted digital ecosystem in the country.
